'''Kelly Paul Oubre Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|uː|b|r|eɪ}} {{respell|OO|bray}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born December 9, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Oubre played one season of college basketball for the [[University of Kansas]] before being selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 15th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]], who then traded him to the [[Washington Wizards]]. Oubre has also played for the [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Charlotte Hornets]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]].

==Early life==
[[File:20140402 MCDAAG Kelly Oubre tomahawk dunk (1).JPG|upright|left|thumb|Oubre during the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Oubre was the second child born in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]], to Kelly Oubre Sr. and Tonya Coleman (formerly Oubre).<ref>http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article3652683.html How KU’s Kelly Oubre rode out a storm and wound up in the Phog – November 17, 2019</ref> Oubre and his family lived in the [[Magnolia Projects|Magnolia]] public housing project from his birth until the early part of his childhood, later settling in the Eastover section of New Orleans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 13, 2017 |title=Slam Online – Nolia Clap: Until Hurricane Katrina forced his family to move to Texas, Wizards forward Kelly Oubre Jr spent the bulk of his childhood bouncing around New Orleans – February 13, 2017 |access-date=December 12, 2017}}</ref> Oubre attended Edward Hynes Elementary School (now known as Hynes Charter School) and played for three Milne Boys Home (now known as New Orleans Recreation Development Commission) basketball teams during that time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Post (Sports) Kelly Oubre Jr. remembers childhood school – February 2017 ==College career==
As a freshman at [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] in 2014–15, Oubre was twice named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Newcomer of the Week<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 19, 2015 |title=KU's Kelly Oubre named Big 12 newcomer of the week |work=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]] |publisher=[[Morris Communications]] |location=[[Topeka, Kansas]] |url=http://cjonline.com/sports/2015-01-19/kus-kelly-oubre-named-big-12-newcomer-week |url-status=live |access-date=January 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123065708/http://cjonline.com/sports/2015-01-19/kus-kelly-oubre-named-big-12-newcomer-week |archive-date=January 23, 2015}}</ref> and subsequently earned All-Newcomer Team honors. He also earned All-Big 12 Honorable Mention honors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2014 |title=Kelly Oubre Jr. – 2014–15 Men's Basketball |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5850 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230082059/http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5850 |archive-date=December 30, 2014 |access-date=November 6, 2014}}</ref> In 36 games (27 starts) for the Jayhawks in 2014–15, Oubre averaged 9.3 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 21.0 minutes per game.

On April 1, 2015, Oubre declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas freshman Oubre declares for '15 NBA Draft |url=http://www.foxsports.com/kansas-city/story/adios-kelly-oubre-kansas-jayhawks-freshman-declares-for-15-nba-draft-040115 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222173652/http://www.foxsports.com/kansas-city/story/adios-kelly-oubre-kansas-jayhawks-freshman-declares-for-15-nba-draft-040115 |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |access-date=December 15, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Washington Wizards (2015–2018)===
[[File:Kelly Oubre Jr. (31653577295).jpg|thumb|right|Oubre jumps for a [[slam dunk]] in 2016]]
Oubre was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 15th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. His draft rights were then traded to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 25, 2015 |title=WIZARDS ACQUIRE KELLY OUBRE JR. IN 2015 NBA DRAFT |url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/06/26/wizards-acquire-kelly-oubre-jr-in-2015-nba-draft |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304095531/http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/06/26/wizards-acquire-kelly-oubre-jr-in-2015-nba-draft |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=June 26, 2015 |website=MonumentalNetwork.com}}</ref> On December 16, 2015, he scored a career-high 18 points on 6-of-15 shooting in a 114–95 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Castillo |first=Jorge |date=December 16, 2015 |title=Wizards stay lost in San Antonio, ending road trip by falling to Spurs |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/wizards-stay-lost-in-san-antonio-ending-road-trip-by-falling-to-spurs/2015/12/16/34660a24-a46a-11e5-9c4e-be37f66848bb_story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044907/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/wizards-stay-lost-in-san-antonio-ending-road-trip-by-falling-to-spurs/2015/12/16/34660a24-a46a-11e5-9c4e-be37f66848bb_story.html |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |access-date=December 10, 2018 |website=WashingtonPost.com}}</ref> Throughout his limited playing time during his rookie season, Oubre showed signs of becoming an effective "3 and D" player.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gehring |first=Chris |date=June 7, 2016 |title=Year in Review: Kelly Oubre |url=https://washingtonwizardsblog.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/06/07/year-in-review-kelly-oubre |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214114311/https://washingtonwizardsblog.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/06/07/year-in-review-kelly-oubre |archive-date=December 14, 2018 |access-date=December 10, 2018 |website=MonumentalNetwork.com}}</ref>

On November 28, 2016, Oubre recorded his first career double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds in a 101–95 overtime win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2016 |title=Beal hits career-high 7 3s, Wizards beat Kings 101–95 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899703 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161129091758/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899703 |archive-date=November 29, 2016 |access-date=November 28, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On December 10, he scored a career-high 19 points to go with nine rebounds and three steals in Washington's 110–105 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2016 |title=Wall, Beal help Wizards use late 11–0 run to beat Bucks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899788 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161211190416/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899788 |archive-date=December 11, 2016 |access-date=December 11, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Oubre was suspended for game four of the Wizards' second-round playoff series against the [[Boston Celtics]] after he was ejected in game three for shoving Boston's [[Kelly Olynyk]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 6, 2017 |title=Kelly Oubre suspended for Game 4 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19323693/kelly-oubre-washington-wizards-suspended-game-4-vs-boston-celtics |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107022615/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19323693/kelly-oubre-washington-wizards-suspended-game-4-vs-boston-celtics |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=November 10, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In 2017–18, Oubre scored over 20 points five times,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kelly Oubre 2017–18 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/oubreke01/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214071224/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/oubreke01/gamelog/2018/ |archive-date=December 14, 2018 |access-date=December 10, 2018 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> including setting a career high with 26 points on January 19 in a 122–112 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=January 19, 2018 |title=Wizards, led by Kelly Oubre Jr., overcome 15-point first-quarter deficit in Detroit |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22157208/kelly-oubre-jr-leads-wizards-road-win-pistons |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120094539/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22157208/kelly-oubre-jr-leads-wizards-road-win-pistons |archive-date=January 20, 2018 |access-date=January 20, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> However, beginning the year shooting 44.9 percent from the field and 40.5 percent from the perimeter through 46 games, Oubre shot just 34.9 percent from the field and 27.4 percent from three in his last 35 games to close the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=Chase |date=May 18, 2018 |title=2017–18 Wizards roster review: Kelly Oubre, Jr. |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/2017-18-wizards-roster-review-kelly-oubre-jr |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214064850/https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/2017-18-wizards-roster-review-kelly-oubre-jr |archive-date=December 14, 2018 |access-date=December 10, 2018 |website=nbcsports.com}}</ref>

On December 10, 2018, Oubre scored a then season-high 23 points in a 109–101 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2018 |title=Turner helps Pacers escape with 109–101 victory over Wizards |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071072 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214070719/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071072 |archive-date=December 14, 2018 |access-date=December 10, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Wizards |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-complete-trade-washington-wizards |url-status=live 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the Suns two days later, scoring 13 points in a 111–103 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2018 |title=Booker, Ayton The injury was later reported as a right meniscus tear.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 27, 2020 |title=Source - Suns' Kelly Oubre could miss rest of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28794718/source-suns-kelly-oubre-miss-rest-season |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228182911/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28794718/source-suns-kelly-oubre-miss-rest-season |archive-date=February 28, 2020 |access-date=March 2, 2020}}</ref> On March 3, 2020, Oubre underwent a successful arthroscopic surgery regarding the torn meniscus in his right knee and would be re-evaluated in four weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2020 |title=Suns' Kelly Oubre Jr. undergoes arthoscopic surgery on knee, out at least four weeks |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/03/03/suns-kelly-oubre-jr-knee-surgery-release |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304020614/https://www.nba.com/article/2020/03/03/suns-kelly-oubre-jr-knee-surgery-release |archive-date=March 4, 2020 |access-date=March 3, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2020–2021)===
On November 16, 2020, Oubre, along with [[Jalen Lecque]], [[Ricky Rubio]], [[Ty Jerome]], and a 2022 first-round draft pick, was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for [[Abdel Nader]] and [[Chris Paul]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2020 |title=Thunder Acquires Ty Jerome, Jalen Lecque, Kelly Oubre Jr., Ricky Rubio and 2022 First-Round Draft Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-201116 |access-date=November 16, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 22, Oubre was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for a conditional 2021 first-round pick and 2021 second-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 22, 2020 |title=Golden State Acquires Kelly Oubre Jr. from Oklahoma City |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-kelly-oubre-20201122 |access-date=November 22, 2020 |website=NBA.com/warriors}}</ref> On December 22, 2020, Oubre made his Warriors debut, putting up six points and seven rebounds in a 125–99 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chua |first=Jeremy |date=December 23, 2020 |title=Warriors PG Stephen Curry's message to Andrew Wiggins, Kelly Oubre Jr. amid awful opener |url=https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-stephen-currys-message-to-andrew-wiggins-kelly-oubre-jr-amid-awful-opener/ |access-date=December 24, 2020 |website=ClutchPoints}}</ref> On February 4, 2021, Oubre scored a career-high 40 points in a 147–116 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2021 |title=Oubre Jr.'s Career-High 40 Points Leads Dubs in 147–116 Shootout Win Over Mavs |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/gameday/20210204/recap |access-date=February 4, 2021 |website=NBA.com/warriors}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2021–2023)===
Oubre signed a 2-year, $25 million contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on August 7, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hornets Sign Kelly Oubre Jr. |work=NBA.com/Hornets |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-kelly-oubre-jr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Warriors SF Kelly Oubre Jr., Hornets Agree to 2-Year, $25M Contract |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2928552-kelly-oubre-jr-hornets-reportedly-finalizing-multiyear-contract-agreement |access-date=March 9, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On October 20, he made his Hornets debut, scoring 14 points in a 123–122 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2021 |title=Ball scores 31 to rally Hornets past Pacers 123–122 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401359833 |access-date=October 20, 2021 |website=ESPN.com |publisher=Associated Press}}</ref> On January 26, 2022, Oubre scored a season-high 39 points and a career-high 10 three-pointers in a 158–126 win over the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marot |first=Michael |date=January 26, 2022 |title=Hornets break franchise record with 158-126 win over Pacers |url=https://apnews.com/article/los-angeles-lakers-charlotte-hornets-indiana-pacers-nba-sports-31f8f9ba95024995c9aa339e215905ba |access-date=November 28, 2022 |website=Associated Press}}</ref>

On November 18, 2022, Oubre scored a season-high 34 points, alongside three rebounds and three steals, in a 132–122 overtime loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CAVALIERS HOLD OFF HORNETS 132-122 IN 2 OVERTIMES, SNAP SKID |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200225 |access-date=April 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 29, he suffered a left hand injury in a 121–113 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=LAMELO BALL HAS 27 POINTS TO HELP HORNETS BEAT THUNDER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200523 |access-date=April 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 5, 2023, Oubre underwent surgery to address a torn ligament in his left hand and was ruled out indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kelly Oubre Jr. Undergoes Successful Surgery |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/kelly-oubre-jr-undergoes-successful-surgery |access-date=April 1, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref> He made his return to action on February 24, recording eight points and three rebounds in a 121–113 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=LAMELO BALL HELPS HORNETS BEAT TIMBERWOLVES 121-113 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200898 |access-date=April 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2023–2026)===
On September 26, 2023, Oubre signed a one-year, $2.9 million deal with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kelly Oubre Jr. Signs with 76ers|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-kelly-oubre-jr|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2023}}</ref> On November 11, Oubre was struck by a car while walking near his [[Center City, Philadelphia|Center City]] residence. He suffered a fractured rib along with injuries to his hip and right leg and was transported to the [[Thomas Jefferson University Hospital]], being released from the hospital after the incident.<ref>{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Pompey|title=Sixers' Kelly Oubre Jr. suffers broken rib, injuries to hip and right leg after getting hit by a car|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-kelly-oubre-hit-by-car-20231111.html|work=Philadelphia Inquirer|date=November 11, 2023|access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref> At the time of the collision, Oubre averaged 16.3 points and 5.1 rebounds per game on 50 percent shooting in 29 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mike|last=McDaniel|title=Sixers Guard Kelly Oubre Hit by Car in Philadelphia, per Report|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/11/12/sixers-guard-kelly-oubre-hit-by-car-in-philadelphia-per-report|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=November 11, 2023|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref> 76ers teammate [[Tyrese Maxey]] would dedicate his 50 points he scored the following day to Oubre following the incident.<ref>{{cite web|first=Karl|last=Rasmussen|title=76ers' Tyrese Maxey Dedicates First-Ever 50-Point Game to Kelly Oubre|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/11/13/76ers-tyrese-maxey-dedicates-first-ever-50-point-game-to-kelly-oubre|website=SI.com|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref> Oubre missed the next 11 games before returning to play on December 6.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ky|last=Carlin|title=Kelly Oubre Jr. reacts to return from injury after Sixers beat Wizards|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2023/12/06/kelly-oubre-jr-reacts-to-return-from-injury-after-sixers-beat-wizards/|work=Sixers Wire|access-date=December 12, 2023}}</ref>
 
On March 29, 2024, Oubre was fined $50,000 for yelling at a referee following a missed call in the 108–107 loss on March 27 to the [[2023–24 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39833345/76ers-nick-nurse-kelly-oubre-jr-fined-yelling-refs 76ers' Nick Nurse, Kelly Oubre Jr. fined for yelling at refs], ESPN, March 29, 2024</ref> 

On July 15, 2024, Oubre was re-signed by the Sixers on a two-year, $16.3 million extension.<ref>{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Re-Sign Kelly Oubre Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-re-sign-kelly-oubre-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 15, 2024}}</ref> On December 30, Oubre put up 15 points, five rebounds, and a career-high eight steals in a 125–103 win over the [[2024–25 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-news-kelly-oubre-sets-new-career-high-not-seen-philadelphia-since-2015|title= 76ers' Kelly Oubre sets new career-high not seen in Philadelphia since 2015|website=ClutchPoints|last=Breisch|first=Matty|date=December 30, 2024|access-date=December 30, 2024}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2026–present)===
On July 8, 2026, Oubre signed a two-year, $17 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Sign Kelly Oubre Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-kelly-oubre-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2026|access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
During his tenure with the Phoenix Suns, Oubre created a brand name of merchandise to help celebrate the community in Arizona and the team that he became a part of for the growth of their future.<ref>[https://arizonasports.com/story/2013604/kelly-oubre-jr-s-wave-of-good-vibes-valley-boyz-movement-return-to-suns/ Kelly Oubre Jr.'s wave of good vibes, Valley Boyz movement return to Suns]</ref><ref>[https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2019/10/18/phoenix-suns-kelly-oubres-valley-boyz-merchandise-set-debut/4019991002/ Kelly Oubre Jr.'s 'Valley Boyz' merchandise available at pop-up shop Saturday]</ref> The "Valley Boyz" name that he came up with for this brand first originated as a hashtag by Oubre on January 9, 2019, as a location tag for the team on [[Instagram]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/suns/tsunami-papis-newest-wave-valley-boyz Tsunami Papi's Newest Wave: The Valley Boyz]</ref> Initial proceeds from the local sales in Phoenix's Uptown Plaza were given to his teammate [[Deandre Ayton]] as proceeds for hurricane relief efforts against [[Hurricane Dorian]] in the Bahamas through [[UNICEF]].<ref>[https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2019/10/20/hundreds-kelly-oubre-jr-valley-boyz-pop-up-shop/4044311002/ Hundreds show up for Phoenix Suns forward Kelly Oubre Jr.'s 'Valley Boyz' pop-up shop]</ref> In addition to the Valley Boyz brand, Oubre also helped design and promote the team's "City Edition" jerseys for the [[2020-21 Phoenix Suns season|2020–21 season]] and [[2021–22 Phoenix Suns season|2021–22 season]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/30277301/how-young-phoenix-suns-got-new-black-valley-jerseys-wanted How the young Phoenix Suns got the new black 'Valley' jerseys they wanted]</ref><ref>[https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2020/11/12/phoenix-suns-representing-the-valley-new-nike-city-edition-jerseys/6266285002/ Phoenix Suns will represent 'The Valley' with new City Edition jerseys]</ref>

Oubre married Shylynn Oubre (née Gibson) in 2022. They have two children together: a daughter, born in 2021, and a son, born in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=England |first=Adam |date=February 20, 2025 |title=Who Is Kelly Oubre Jr.'s Wife? All About Shylynn Oubre and Her Relationship with the Philadelphia 76ers Guard |url=https://people.com/who-is-shylynn-oubre-kelly-oubre-jr-wife-8788144}}</ref>

On November 11, 2023, Oubre was a pedestrian in center city Philadelphia and was struck by a [[hit and run]] driver. He was treated for a broken rib among various other injuries, and released from a local hospital.<ref>[https://6abc.com/sports/76ers-guard-kelly-oubre-jr-struck-injured-by-vehicle-in-philadelphia/14046473/ 76ers guard Kelly Oubre Jr. struck, injured by vehicle in Philadelphia]</ref>

In the early morning of April 23, 2024, Oubre was involved in a second automobile-related accident, disregarding a red light and subsequently striking another vehicle, though no injuries would result from the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |date=April 25, 2024 |title=Kelly Oubre Jr. Involved in Car Crash After 76ers' Game 2 Loss to Knicks |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10118590-kelly-oubre-jr-involved-in-car-crash-after-76ers-game-2-loss-to-knicks |access-date=2024-10-19 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>
